name: supertrend_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: SuperTrend is the single most-watched indicator among Indian retail traders — Zerodha, Angel One, and Groww all feature it prominently, and millions of NIFTY intraday traders use SuperTrend(10, 3.0) on 1-minute charts as their primary buy/sell signal. When SuperTrend flips from red (resistance) to green (support) on NIFTY, a massive wave of retail market orders floods in within 10-30 seconds as these traders enter simultaneously. This is a SECOND-ORDER trade: we are not trading the SuperTrend signal itself (which is a lagging ATR-based trend indicator), but rather the predictable CROWD BEHAVIOR that the signal triggers. At 5-second resolution, we compute SuperTrend(120, 3.0) which represents the same 10-minute period as the original 1-min(10) calculation. The edge is in the 30-60 second window after the flip: retail order flow creates genuine momentum that ATM options capture at 2-5 points before the flow subsides. The flip itself is detectable the INSTANT it happens at 5s resolution — 55 seconds before it would appear on a 1-minute chart — giving us a structural timing advantage over the millions of traders watching 1-minute bars.

indicators.name: atr_120
indicators.purpose: 120-bar ATR on 5s bars = 10-minute ATR, matching the original SuperTrend(10) on 1-min bars. 10 minutes is the sweet spot because it captures NIFTY's intraday swing rhythm — shorter ATR periods (e.g., 2-3 min) flip too frequently on noise, longer periods (20+ min) flip too slowly to generate the sudden retail herding effect. The 10-minute period is specifically chosen because it matches what millions of retail traders actually use on their 1-minute charts.

indicators.name: supertrend_120
indicators.formula: SuperTrend(120, 3.0): upper_band = HL2 + 3.0 * ATR(120), lower_band = HL2 - 3.0 * ATR(120), with trailing logic
indicators.purpose: The core SuperTrend indicator. Multiplier 3.0 is the default used by the vast majority of retail traders — this is critical because we need OUR SuperTrend to flip at the exact same moment as theirs. Using a different multiplier would desynchronize us from the crowd signal. The 120-bar lookback on 5s bars replicates the 10-bar lookback on 1-min bars that retail traders see.

indicators.name: supertrend_flip
indicators.formula: 1 if supertrend_120 direction changed this bar (from bearish to bullish or vice versa), else 0
indicators.purpose: Binary flip detector. The flip is the EVENT we trade — not the trend direction itself. At 5s resolution, we detect the flip up to 55 seconds before 1-minute chart users see it, giving us a first-mover advantage into the retail flow wave.

indicators.name: ret_24
indicators.purpose: 2-minute return as a pre-flip momentum filter. A SuperTrend flip preceded by a 2-minute move of 0.05%+ in the flip direction indicates genuine directional pressure (not a whipsaw). 2 minutes is long enough to distinguish real moves from noise on NIFTY but short enough to still be within the early phase of the trend.

conditions: supertrend_flip == 1 AND new direction is BULLISH (SuperTrend flipped from resistance to support)
ret_24 > 0.03 (NIFTY has been moving up for the last 2 minutes — confirms the flip is with momentum, not a false flip in chop)
Time is not within 5 minutes of a previous SuperTrend flip (avoid whipsaw zones where SuperTrend flips back and forth)
buy_ce.confirmation: Entry on the SAME bar as the flip — no delay, because the retail flow starts immediately and we need to be ahead of it

conditions: supertrend_flip == 1 AND new direction is BEARISH (SuperTrend flipped from support to resistance)
ret_24 < -0.03 (NIFTY has been moving down for the last 2 minutes)
Time is not within 5 minutes of a previous SuperTrend flip
buy_pe.confirmation: Entry on the same bar as the flip

exit.stop_rationale: If the SuperTrend flip fails to generate retail momentum within the first 15-30 seconds, price typically reverses the flip within 1 minute (the flip was a false signal in choppy conditions). A 4-point stop on NIFTY ATM options corresponds to roughly 8 spot points, which is the typical noise band during a false SuperTrend flip. This gives the trade just enough room to survive initial noise but exits before a full reversal develops.
exit.target_rationale: When a SuperTrend flip on NIFTY triggers genuine retail herding, the resulting momentum delivers 15-30 spot points over 30-90 seconds (7-15 ATM option points). Target of 7 captures the conservative end of this range — roughly the first 30-45 seconds of retail flow before counter-trend algos start fading the move. Risk-reward is 1:1.75, appropriate for a ~50% win-rate momentum trade.

filters.vix_filter: none — retail herding on SuperTrend flips occurs in all VIX regimes. Higher VIX amplifies the move magnitude but does not change the crowd behavior pattern.
filters.time_filter: No trades before 09:20 (opening auction noise causes false SuperTrend flips) or after 15:20 (retail traders reduce activity near close). Avoid first 5 minutes after market open when SuperTrend is still initializing.
filters.volume_filter: none — we are trading the crowd signal, not volume patterns
filters.trend_filter: ret_24 serves as a lightweight momentum confirmation that the flip direction aligns with recent price action
filters.spread_filter: skip if ATM option bid-ask > 2 points (tight spread needed because we enter aggressively on the flip bar)
filters.whipsaw_filter: No entry within 60 bars (5 minutes) of a previous SuperTrend flip — frequent flips indicate range-bound conditions where retail herding cancels out

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — the edge derives from millions of retail traders watching SuperTrend, which is deeply embedded in Indian trading culture. This behavior is unlikely to change unless SuperTrend falls out of favor as a retail indicator.

adaptation_notes: Original traded SuperTrend(10, 3.0) on 1-min bars with 10-30 minute holds as a straightforward trend-following signal. The 5s adaptation fundamentally reframes the trade: instead of treating SuperTrend as a trend indicator (which it is, poorly, on an index), we treat the SuperTrend FLIP as an EVENT that triggers predictable crowd behavior. Lookback scaled from 10 bars at 1-min to 120 bars at 5s (10 min / 5s = 120), preserving the exact time horizon retail traders see. Multiplier kept at 3.0 (NOT adjusted) because synchronization with the retail crowd is the entire edge. Added ret_24 momentum filter (not in original) because at 5s resolution we see many more false flips than on 1-min bars — the momentum filter eliminates flips that occur in noise without directional backing. Hold time compressed from 10-30 minutes to 30-120 seconds because we only want the INITIAL retail flow burst, not the subsequent trend (which is what the original traded). Stop compressed from the original's implied ~30 spot points to 4 option points because our hold is 10-15x shorter.
weaknesses: SuperTrend whipsaws frequently in range-bound NIFTY sessions, generating 4-6 false flips per day that all hit stops
The 5s SuperTrend flip can occur up to 55s before the 1-min flip — but if it then flips BACK before the 1-min bar closes, the retail wave never materializes
Crowding risk: if other algos start front-running SuperTrend flips the same way, the edge compresses as entry prices worsen
During low-liquidity periods (lunch hours), the retail flow from SuperTrend flips is insufficient to move NIFTY meaningfully
